claims.summary: Atlas Rewind captures picture-only screen frames with consent; hosted submission to F7 is planned and not built
evidence: public-docs: content/legal/privacy-policy.md — the Atlas Rewind subsection: picture-only capture, no audio, the per-capture model read, and submission labelled planned and not built
public-docs: content/privacy/data-collection.md — the 'Data Never Captured' guarantees are scoped to the F7 agent and point at the Rewind subsection
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/lib/rewind-config.ts — capture is picture-only at a fixed frame rate
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/lib/build-profile.ts — the recorder is reachable only on a development server or an internal reference build, so no customer deployment shows it

fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/components/RewindFirstRun.tsx — the in-product explainer states picture-only capture, no audio, and that asking for a read sends that capture's stills and words to the configured model provider
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/legal/privacy-policy.md — the in-app policy's Rewind section, which this page must agree with
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/legal/terms-of-use.md — the consent clause: recorded against the deployment, revocable, never implied by a plan or licence tier

NOTE: the hosted submission path is designed and NOT built — no submit path exists in any shipped build and no customer deployment has been granted the recorder, so every sentence about submitting is labelled planned both on the page and here
claims.notes: Registered ahead of the feature by deliberate rule: the privacy policy and every public surface describing Rewind must be updated before any customer sees the recorder, so this claim exists while the control is still partly planned. TRUE TODAY: capture is picture-only with no audio; a capture stays on the customer's own Atlas instance; the one egress that exists is the reviewer asking a model to read the frames they selected, consented per capture; and the recorder is absent from every customer deployment. PLANNED, and must not be answered as a current control on a vendor questionnaire: submitting a capture to F7, and everything a submission carries. Retention of a submitted capture is deliberately unsettled: it was left to legal review on 2026-09-09 rather than fixed internally, so the page states that it is not yet set and will be stated before submission is offered, rather than publishing a period no counsel has approved and no code enforces. Who at F7 may open a submitted capture was ruled on 2026-09-09: state today's answer as today's and leave the hosted answer to the work that builds the submission path. The page therefore states the narrow answer that is true now (only the reviewer who recorded it, because Rewind runs on F7 internal builds only) and does not present it as a promise that survives submission being built. soc2_criteria is deliberately empty until submission is built and counsel has reviewed the clause; mapping a partly planned control to a trust service criterion would overstate it. PUBDOC-4 is the public-docs claim review that introduced this entry and should be renamed to the audit finding that supersedes it. This is also the first mention of Atlas anywhere on the public site.
